documents.title: Office Visit - Contraception
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to talk about birth control. About two months into a new relationship, having sex with this partner, and they haven't been using anything reliably. She wants to avoid pregnancy and is also worried about infections since she doesn't know his testing history.

Cycles regular. LMP roughly two weeks ago. Never pregnant. No prior STI. No meds, NKDA. FH noncontributory. Doesn't smoke, drink or use drugs.
GU ROS: no discharge, no pelvic pain, no burning with urination.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pelvic exam with chaperone: external genitalia normal, vaginal walls and cervix normal, no discharge, no cervical motion tenderness, uterus and adnexa normal size and nontender. Swabs collected.

Assessment and plan: Contraceptive counseling. Went through the options: pill, patch, ring, injection, implant and IUDs, plus condoms. Explained that only condoms also lower STI risk, and that pairing condoms with a second method is the most protective against pregnancy. She prefers to start with condoms alone for now and use them every time; open to adding a hormonal method later. Encouraged her partner to get tested. Gave information on emergency contraception available over the counter.
GC/CT NAAT sent today.
Return any time to revisit.

documents.title: Test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christine, chlamydia and gonorrhea were both negative. Let me know if you'd like to talk about adding another method.
